title: Why he disliked recording with singers
summary: He found singers fussy and the repeated takes tiresome.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: See, I was working what you call gigs, a lot of gigs. Work here one night, work here one night. Before I went with Fletcher, because Honey Potter, he worked mostly on the weekends. But during the week I worked gigs. So it's quite possible, but I didn't like to work with singers, record with singers. I didn't, because you had to make so many trials before you made that master, you had to go over it again and go over it again, and the singer, sometimes they were fussy, they didn't like this and that, and the band -- you knew what you were playing, but it was the singer. They didn't like this and they didn't like that, they don't like that, and, oh, boy.

(Inaudible) so fussy about it for? Why don't we get this thing over with? Then they'd have to make another one, and finally they'd say, there's the master, you'll make the master now. You make the master and that's the end of it. But you'd be there, just playing over and over and over and over again, for this old singer.
Yeah, that's true. Because experienced musicians, they knew the song. Yeah, they knew it. They knew it from A to Z. Well, anyhow, to get back to Duke.
